## Context

- The most-copied code shape: thousands of builtins. A change after the freeze touches all of them [R07: Brimstone's handle refactor].
- Depends on: H10 (CSS keeps Rust locals alive), H14 (frame layout: `Args` reads the host frame), H06 (`Value` wraps `NonZeroU64`), H19 (atoms are the property keys), H22 (realms, R5). Depended on by: the builtins (P2, P3), H13 (BuiltinId index list), H35 (unit link cells), the JIT and AOT host-call stub.

## Decision

Plan row (02 §6): `fn(cx, this, args, new_target) -> JsResult<Local<'s>>`. `Args` is a frame view; `Throw` is a ZST; no `&mut` to a heap object across a JS call. AOT code reaches builtins through the isolate table or the link table. The row said `-> JsResult<Value>` until the v1 draft put `Local` in place of `Value` (a rewrite of the row's result type before the freeze; P4-DOCS updated 02 in 6bebbb1, M0 wk4):

```rust
pub type HostFn = for<'s> fn(&mut Cx<'s>, Local<'s>, Args<'s>, Local<'s>) -> JsResult<Local<'s>>;
//                           cx           this       args (= fp)  new_target
```

| Type | What it is | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `Cx<'s>` | the context: ObjectOps, conversions, calls, `throw_*`; exposes no `&Runtime` | `crates/ep9_vm/src/abi/mod.rs:510` |
| `Local<'s, T>` | the value itself, `repr(transparent)` over `Value`; `Copy`, `!Send`, `!Sync`; markers `JsValue` (default), `JsObject`, `JsFunction`, `JsArray`, `JsString`, `FlatStr`, `JsSymbol`, `JsKey`; checked downcasts, `From` upcasts | `crates/ep9_vm/src/abi/local.rs:147` |
| `Args<'s>` | one word, the host frame pointer: `len`, `get`, `this`, `new_target`, `callee`, `rest(i)` | `crates/ep9_vm/src/abi/mod.rs:101` |
| `PropertyDescriptor<'s>` | §6.2.6, every field optional | `crates/ep9_vm/src/abi/mod.rs:230` |
| `ScratchList<'s>` | LIFO precise list over `ep9_heap::ScratchRoots` | `crates/ep9_vm/src/abi/mod.rs:379` |
| `ArgsBuilder<'s>` | call arguments on the VM stack above the frame top, under the scratch top (no heap list) | `crates/ep9_vm/src/abi/mod.rs:410` |
| `IteratorRecord<'s>` | an Iterator Record (§7.4.1): `iterator()`, `next_method()`, `is_done()`; stack-only (R2) because it holds `Local`s | `crates/ep9_vm/src/abi/iter.rs:30` |
| `PromiseCapability<'s>` | a PromiseCapability Record (§27.2.1.1): `promise`, `resolve`, `reject`; stack-only (R2) because it holds `Local`s | `crates/ep9_vm/src/abi/jobs.rs:78` |

**ObjectOps v0** (`Cx` methods, spec names): `get`, `get_v`, `set`, `has_property`, `has_own_property`, `get_own_property`, `define_own_property` (ValidateAndApplyPropertyDescriptor), `define_property_or_throw`, `create_data_property(_or_throw)`, `delete`, `delete_property_or_throw`, `own_property_keys` (a JS array: indices ascending, strings in creation order, symbols), `get/set_prototype_of`, `is_extensible`, `prevent_extensions`, `is_callable`, `is_constructor`, `is_array`. Conversions: `to_boolean`, `to_number`, `to_integer_or_infinity`, `to_int32`, `to_uint32`, `to_length`, `to_string`, `to_property_key`, `to_object`, `to_primitive`, `same_value`, `is_strictly_equal`. Spec helpers: `to/from_property_descriptor`, `create_list_from_array_like` (into an `ArgsBuilder`), `get_prototype_from_constructor`, `ordinary_create_from_constructor` (a `prototype` that is not an object falls back to the default intrinsic of GetFunctionRealm(constructor), §10.1.14 step 4). Creation: `new_object(_with_proto)`, `new_array`, `create_array_from_list`, `new_string(_utf16)`, `new_wrapper`, `new_symbol`, `intrinsic(IntrinsicId)`. P3 surface (P2-BTAB): `symbol_for`, `key_for`, `symbol_description`, `descriptive_string`, `this_primitive_value(v, PrimitiveType)`, `set_function_name`, `set_function_length`, `new_bound_function(target, this, args.rest(i))`, `has_intrinsic`, `initial_name(f) -> Option<Local<JsString>>` (the `[[InitialName]]` of a host function, from its FunctionInfo; `None` for bytecode and bound functions; an accessor's functions are named "get x" / "set x"; W4-P3FIX-INITIAL-NAME). Calls: `call`, `call_args(f, this, args.rest(i))`, `call_built`, `construct(f, args, new_target)` with any constructor as new.target, `construct_args`, `construct_built`. **Index access** (ABI-1, `crates/ep9_vm/src/abi/index.rs`): `get_index(o, k)`, `has_index(o, k)`, `set_index(o, k, v, throw)` and `delete_index(o, k, throw)` are Get, HasProperty, Set and `[[Delete]]` / DeletePropertyOrThrow with the key `! ToString(𝔽(k))` for a `u64` `k`. A dense element and a missing index need no key, so they make no atom; a stored integer key of an object with at most 64 own properties is found by a scan (the array index from the atom's hash field, or the digits); otherwise the key is interned and the ordinary path runs (`property::get_index` and its neighbours, `crates/ep9_vm/src/property.rs:2106`). A missing array index stops at the receiver while no prototype has an index key (`shape::proto_index_keys`). `poll_interrupt()` takes one interrupt budget unit and polls when it runs out (termination gives an uncatchable `Err(Throw)`): a builtin loop over indices has no back edge, so it calls it once per index. **Iterator protocol** (ABI-3, `crates/ep9_vm/src/abi/iter.rs`): `get_iterator(obj)` (GetIterator, sync; the async form comes later as an addition), `get_iterator_from_method(obj, method)`, `iterator_step_value(&mut record) -> Option<Local>` (a throw or done sets `[[Done]]`; one interrupt budget unit per step) and `iterator_close(&record, completion)` (a throw completion keeps its exception whatever `return` does). Accessor properties are built (P3-ACC). v0 limits: these throw "not implemented" until H18 element storage: an accessor on an array index, an array element whose attributes are not {w, e, c}, and a non-writable array `length` (W4-ACC-ELEM).

**Internal slots** (ABI-SLOTS, `crates/ep9_vm/src/abi/slots.rs`): `new_object_with_slots(proto, class, n)`, `slot(o, class, i)`, `set_slot(o, class, i, v)` and `object_class(v)`. The class decides what each slot index means, and its builtin module names the indices. Slots hold Values in a heap cell (plan rule 8), and property code never touches them. A slot index past the count panics.

**JIT and AOT** never call a `HostFn` (Rust ABI). They call one `extern "C"` host-call stub `(cx, fp) -> bits` that pushes the host frame and runs `call::call_host`; the builtin is named by its FunctionInfo or its `BuiltinId` (block 7 bits + index 9 bits) through the isolate table or a unit link cell (H35).

### Builtin tables (M0 wk4 P2)

```text
IsolateConfig { builtins: Some(&ep9_builtins::TABLE), .. }
Isolate::new
  builtins::check      both tables pass check_tables (cached per table)  -> IsolateError::BuiltinTable
  Runtime::new
  builtins::prepare    one dense FunctionInfo array + one root range of function slots per module
  realm::init          atoms; core intrinsics: %Object.prototype%, %Function.prototype% (VM builtin 0.0),
                       Array/String/Number/Boolean/Iterator/ArrayIterator/Error prototypes, the global
  builtins::install    VM table (block 0), then the embedder table, modules in order:
                       pass 1 every function object; pass 2 the intrinsics; pass 3 the properties
```

| Type | What it is | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `BuiltinId(u16)` | block (7 bits, < 128) + index (9 bits, < 512): definition `i` of the module with block `b`. Blocks are fixed per module; ids are append-only | `crates/ep9_vm/src/builtins.rs:53` |
| `IntrinsicId` | 72 append-only ids: the core prototypes 0-16 (made by realm init; `SymbolPrototype` by `symbol::install`), the constructors and `%Math%` 17-31 (made by tables), `%StringIteratorPrototype%` 32 (made by the VM table), `%GeneratorFunction%`, its prototype, `%GeneratorPrototype%`, `%AsyncFunction%`, its prototype and `%eval%` 33-38 (the VM table), then `%Promise%`, `%Promise.prototype%`, `%AggregateError%` and `%AggregateError.prototype%` 39-42 (`ep9_builtins` promise.rs, M2-P4), `%Reflect%` 43 (`ep9_builtins` reflect.rs, M2-P5), `%Array.prototype%[@@unscopables]` 44 (the VM table natives.rs, M2-P5 VM-SMALL), and ids 45-63 declared in M3-P0 for the month-3 builders (P0-D3): `%AsyncGeneratorFunction%`, its prototype, `%AsyncGeneratorPrototype%`, `%AsyncIteratorPrototype%`, `%AsyncFromSyncIteratorPrototype%` 45-49 (the VM table, M3-P2 ASYNCGEN); `%Date%`, `%Date.prototype%` 50-51 (`ep9_builtins` date.rs, M3-P1); `%Map%`, `%Set%`, `%WeakMap%`, `%WeakSet%` and their prototypes 52-59, `%MapIteratorPrototype%`, `%SetIteratorPrototype%` 60-61 (collections.rs, M3-P1); `%JSON%` 62 (json.rs, M3-P1, an ordinary object with `%Object.prototype%`); `%ThrowTypeError%` 63 (the VM table, M3-P2 VM-ARGS step 2); and ids 64-71 declared in M4-P0 for the month-4 builders (plan v9 rule 18): `%Proxy%` 64 (`ep9_builtins` proxy.rs, M5-P3 PROXY2), `%RegExp%`, `%RegExp.prototype%`, `%RegExpStringIteratorPrototype%` 65-67 (`ep9_builtins` regexp.rs, M4-P3 REGEXP1), `%WeakRef%`, `%WeakRef.prototype%`, `%FinalizationRegistry%`, `%FinalizationRegistry.prototype%` 68-71 (`ep9_builtins` weakref.rs, M4-P4 WEAKREF). Each maps to a runtime root, except `SymbolPrototype` (kept by `symbol.rs`) and ids 32-71, which are slots 0-39 of the isolate's builtin state (W4-NAT-STRITER-PROTO; `IntrinsicId::slot`) | `crates/ep9_vm/src/builtins.rs:103` |
| `BuiltinDef` | `{name, length, kind: Method \| Getter \| Setter \| Constructor, f: HostFn}`; a getter is named "get x" | `crates/ep9_vm/src/builtins.rs:823` |
| `PropDef` | `{key, value, attrs}`. Key: `Atom` (the `atoms!` list), `Str` (interned at init), `Symbol` (well-known). Value: `Builtin(i)`, `Intrinsic`, `Const`, `Symbol`, `Alias(key)` (the value of a key defined earlier on the same object: one function object under two names), `Accessor {get, set}` | `crates/ep9_vm/src/builtins.rs:1048` |
| `BuiltinModule`, `IntrinsicDef`, `ObjectProps` | a module: name, block, `defs`, the intrinsics it makes (`Builtin(i)` or a new ordinary object), the properties per target intrinsic | `crates/ep9_vm/src/builtins.rs:1128` |
| `BuiltinTable` | a name and its modules; `check_tables` checks a list of tables | `crates/ep9_vm/src/builtins.rs:1207`, `crates/ep9_vm/src/builtins.rs:1257` |

`check_tables` rejects: a block ≥ 128 or used twice; more than 512 definitions; an intrinsic made twice, or a core one made other than as a VM builtin; a property on, or a reference to, an intrinsic nothing makes; a definition index out of range or of the wrong kind (`Builtin` needs a Method or Constructor, `Accessor` a Getter/Setter); an `Alias` of a key not defined earlier on the same object; a key defined twice on one object. It also rejects a table that makes `IntrinsicId::RealmFuses` (id 72; "[[RealmFuses]] is VM-internal: no table makes it"): the realm's fuse block is a FUSE cell (kind 83) that realm init makes (`fuse::new_realm_block`), not an object, and a table's object would replace it in `Root::RealmFuses` (M6-P2 integration fixer, a rewrite of this Frozen core rule, Change log 2026-11-04). A constructor that a table makes must get `prototype` ({} attributes) as its first table key, and must get one (W4-BTAB-CTOR-PROTO-FIRST); the one exception is `%Proxy%`, which has no `prototype` (§28.2.2): `check_tables` takes it with none, and `exotic::is_lazy_prototype` makes none for it (M5-P3 PROXY2, a rewrite of this Frozen core rule, Change log 2026-10-29). Install also refuses, in every build, a key the target already has (a function's own `length`/`name`, or anything realm init made), with `IsolateError::BuiltinTable` (W4-BTAB-INSTALL-NO-SECOND-KEY). Install errors (a well-known symbol or an accessor that does not exist yet) fail `Isolate::new` with a message naming the module and key.

**One function object per builtin and realm.** `builtins::function_object` makes it on first use and keeps it in the module's root slot (the first realm) or in the install list while a later realm installs (`builtins::begin_realm_install`), so an `Alias`, an intrinsic and a property name one object in each realm. Every realm's function object of a definition shares its FunctionInfo. The FunctionInfos sit in one boxed slice per module (no Box per function); `rt.infos` keeps only embedder host functions. [2026-11-06, M7-P1 LAZYNS (INTL-I1-D8; the lazy install that M3-PLAN-D7 deferred; fill):] A lazy group is not installed at realm init. The group of a key of a private list (`Temporal`, `Intl`; a key with no module does nothing) is the module that puts the key on `%GlobalObject%`, then each module whose props target only group intrinsics or its own intrinsics; it is computed once per table. At realm init the key gets its table place and attributes with the value HOLE (its field at rep ANY, not const), the group's intrinsics stay undefined in the REALM record, and the group's FunctionInfos are not made. `builtins::install_group` installs the group, in table order, into the realm that owns the key at the first use there: a read that finds HOLE on a realm's global object (`[[Get]]`, `[[GetOwnProperty]]`, `[[DefineOwnProperty]]` and the global load miss), or an intrinsic use (`Cx::intrinsic`, `Cx::get_prototype_from_constructor`, `Cx::function_realm_intrinsic` and its `try_` form, through `realm::intrinsic_for_use`). It writes the key only while the key still holds HOLE, so a write, a define or a delete before the first use keeps its eager result. `[[Set]]`, `[[Delete]]`, HasProperty and `[[OwnPropertyKeys]]` do not install. `Cx::has_intrinsic` answers true for a lazy id from the group map, with no install (no new GC point); `builtins::intrinsic` stays a raw read. Two rules for later readers: (MC-w30-3) a unit link step installs the group of a lazy IntrinsicRef id first, or uses the id only as an identity guard; (MC-w30-4) a compiled or unit reader whose fact was not recorded in this realm after the install treats HOLE as a miss, as the lexical path does (`ic::global_case_value`). No name, signature, id or golden line changes.

**Ids are golden-checked.** `crates/ep9_vm/tests/golden/vm-builtin-ids.txt` (the VM module plus the `IntrinsicId` list) and `crates/ep9_builtins/tests/golden/ids-<module>.txt` hold one line per definition; a reorder fails them, and `EP9_BLESS=1` rewrites them after a review that sees only appended lines.

**The VM table** (`crates/ep9_vm/src/natives.rs:737`, block 0): `%Function.prototype%` (a function that returns undefined, §20.2.3), `Function` (CreateDynamicFunction, §20.2.1.1, through the compiler hook `compile_function`, `crates/ep9_vm/src/abi/script.rs`; an EvalError on an isolate without hooks), `Object` (new.target, then `to_object`, §20.1.1.1), `Array`, the 7 error constructors, `Object.prototype.toString`/`valueOf` (`toString` gives the builtinTag "Arguments" for an arguments object, mapped or unmapped, §20.1.3.6 step 5; M3-P2 VM-ARGS step 2), `Array.prototype.join`/`toString`/`push` (`push` is generic: a non-Array `this` takes the spec steps, §23.1.3.23), `Array.prototype.values` (also `Array.prototype[@@iterator]`, one function object), `Array.prototype.keys`/`entries` (VM ids 0.28, 0.29; M2-P4 B-ARRAY), `%ArrayIteratorPrototype%.next`, `String.prototype[@@iterator]`, `%StringIteratorPrototype%` with its `next` and `@@toStringTag` "String Iterator", `%Iterator.prototype%[@@iterator]`, the `%Iterator.prototype%[@@toStringTag]` accessor (get "Iterator", set SetterThatIgnoresPrototypeProperties; VM ids 0.31, 0.32), `Function.prototype[@@hasInstance]` (OrdinaryHasInstance; VM id 0.30), the `%Array.prototype%[@@unscopables]` object (`IntrinsicId` 44) (all three M2-P5 VM-SMALL), `Error.prototype.toString`, `%GeneratorFunction%` (through the compiler hook like `Function`), the `%GeneratorPrototype%` methods `next`, `return` and `throw`, `%AsyncFunction%` (CreateDynamicFunction of kind async through the compiler hook, M3-P1 ASYNC; its fallback prototype is `%AsyncFunction.prototype%` of GetFunctionRealm(newTarget), `abi/script.rs`), the async-generator builtins of M3-P2 ASYNCGEN (VM ids 0.33-0.40: `%AsyncGeneratorFunction%`, length 1, through the compiler hook like `Function`, its fallback prototype `%AsyncGeneratorFunction.prototype%` of GetFunctionRealm(newTarget); the `%AsyncGeneratorPrototype%` methods `next`, `return` and `throw`, length 1; `%AsyncIteratorPrototype%[@@asyncIterator]`, length 0; the `%AsyncFromSyncIteratorPrototype%` methods `next`, `return` and `throw`, length 1; with them the VM table makes `IntrinsicId` 45-49), `%ThrowTypeError%` (VM id 0.41, a method with length 0 and name "", `IntrinsicId` 63; M3-P2 VM-ARGS step 2, M3D-2: the `callee` accessor of an unmapped arguments object, §10.4.4.6 step 9, §10.2.4.1; on first use in a realm `crates/ep9_vm/src/arguments.rs` makes its `length` and `name` {w: false, e: false, c: false} and the function non-extensible; a call throws a TypeError), the global `eval` (`%eval%`, indirect eval, §19.2.1; direct eval is `crates/ep9_vm/src/interp/slow/eval.rs`), and the globals `globalThis`, `undefined`, `NaN`, `Infinity`. [2026-11-07, M7-P2 integration fixer (SPEC-D F1, form B by M6-ORCH-191; fill):] the `%Function.prototype%` accessors `caller` and `arguments` (§10.2.4 AddRestrictedFunctionProperties; {e: false, c: true}): one getter (VM id 0.42, "get caller", length 0) and one setter (VM id 0.43, "set caller", length 1) for both keys (`natives::restricted_function_property`). A non-strict ordinary function gets undefined from the getter, and the setter does nothing for it; every other receiver gets the TypeError of `%ThrowTypeError%` (§10.2.4.1). So the halves are not `%ThrowTypeError%` itself: this is the web-legacy form of V8, SpiderMonkey and JavaScriptCore, and test262 `prop-desc.js` of `caller` and `arguments` and `ThrowTypeError/unique-per-realm-function-proto.js` fail on it, as on those engines.

**Crate layout.** `ep9_builtins` (engine dependencies ep9_vm and ep9_math, and [2026-11-06, spec-int fixer (checker F1), the H20:301 rewrite of spec-temporal T1] ep9_temporal for the Temporal modules (dep-guards check 8), and [2026-11-07, INTL W1 CORE (INTL-I1-D1, layout B), the rewrite row of 2026-11-07] ep9_intl for the Intl modules (dep-guards checks 8 and 24; ep9_intl depends on ep9_vm and ep9_temporal), `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`) has one file per module, each with `BLOCK`, `DEFS`, `INTRINSICS`, `PROPS` and `MODULE`: object 1, function 2, array 3, number 4, boolean 5, string 6, symbol 7, math 8, global 9, promise 10, reflect 11, date 12, collections 13, json 14. `TABLE` lists them in that order, which is the property order. Its `clippy.toml` repeats the root bans (clippy reads only the nearest file) and adds `disallowed-types`: `ep9_value::Value`, `Unpacked`, `Word0` and the ep9_heap cell types (re-exports such as `ep9_vm::Value` resolve to them). `TEMPLATES.md` is the writing guide, and its code blocks are doctests. `ep9_cli` and `tools/test262` pass `TABLE`; test262 `exec` exits 2 when an isolate has no table.

**Embedders get `Local` too** (H20-Q4, filled in M3-P3): `Isolate::with_cx(|cx| ...)` runs a closure with a `Cx`; the `for<'s>` bound keeps every `Local` inside it (a `compile_fail` doctest proves the escape does not compile). `Isolate::with_cx_checkpoint(|cx| ...)` is the same scope, then a microtask checkpoint (also after a throw): a host runs a script or a call in it. The scoped forms of the old `Value` API are `Cx` methods (M0 month 2 P3, C11; `crates/ep9_vm/src/isolate.rs:916`): `run_script(unit, file) -> JsResult<Local>` (loads and runs a unit), `global_binding(name) -> JsResult<Option<Local>>` (GetBindingValue of the global environment: the lexical record first, a binding in its TDZ throws a ReferenceError, then HasProperty and `[[Get]]` on the global object, so a getter runs; `None` = unresolvable) and `display(v) -> String` (runs no JS). The scoped call is the existing `call`, and `global()` keeps its signature. `evaluate_script(source, file) -> JsResult<Local>` (M0 month 2 P3-EVAL-VM, `crates/ep9_vm/src/abi/script.rs:65`) compiles a source string as a sloppy Script through the compiler hook `compile_script` and runs it as `run_script` does (`this` = the global object; an EvalError on an isolate without hooks). A `compile_fail` doctest per new form shows that its `Local` cannot leave `with_cx`. `Isolate::with_module_host(resolve, load, f)` (M3-P3 EMBED-MIGRATE) puts the module host hooks in place for `import()` in all the code that runs during `f` (the Modules row). The raw `Isolate::{run_script, call, global, display}` were removed in M3-P3 (EMBED-MIGRATE). `Isolate::heap(&self) -> &Heap` also gave raw `Value`s to safe code (Codex W4-1): `Heap::alloc`, `Heap::find_cell` and `Heap::last_conservative_roots` give `CellPtr`s, and `CellPtr::to_value` makes a `Value` that no scope keeps live. M3-P3 fix round 5 put it in an `impl Isolate` block under `cfg(any(test, feature = "spike-native"))`, so the default build has no `Isolate::heap`; `Isolate::gc_stats(&self) -> GcStats` (a copy of the counters) took its 3 callers outside `ep9_vm` (`ep9_cli --gc-stats` and 2 `ep9_builtins` tests). Now no default-build `Isolate` method takes or gives a raw `Value` or a type whose safe methods give one (`Heap`, `CellPtr`, `ScratchRoots`, `Slot`), except `string_view`, which checks its `Value` (below; H20-Q4). **The embedder entry points are core** (M3-P3 FREEZE-PREP step 2; fix round 5, Codex W4-3; fix round 6, RV5-F3). One test: an entry point is an `Isolate` method that runs ABI code (a `Cx` scope, JS or a `HostFn`), or that takes a hook, a function of the embedder that is called while ABI code runs. The 8 entry points are `with_cx`, `with_cx_checkpoint`, `create_realm`, `perform_microtask_checkpoint`, `take_unhandled_rejections` (the message of a reason that is an object but not an Error is ToString(reason), which can call JS or a `HostFn`; its doctest shows a `HostFn` `toString` that runs in the call), `new` (`IsolateConfig` gives it 3 kinds of hooks: the builtin tables, whose `HostFn`s ABI code calls; the `PromiseRejectionTracker`; and the `CompilerHooks`, which `Cx::evaluate_script` (`abi/script.rs`), `eval` and `Function()` call), `register_host_function` (it takes a `HostFn`) and `with_module_host` (it takes the `resolve` and `load` hooks that `import()` calls; like the compiler hooks, they get no `Cx`). With the path `ep9_vm::Isolate`, they are lines of the core golden (`embed: impl Isolate ::` lines; test `the_golden_has_the_embedder_entry_points`). `Isolate::compiler()` gives the compiler hooks back and takes none, so it is not an entry point. The types that the entry points name are core lines too (fix round 6, RV5-F2; decision M3-P3-H20-CORETYPES): the golden reads them to the end (the type closure), so `Exception`, `SourceLocation`, `IsolateError`, `IsolateConfig` (each pub field, its `Default` impl and `DEFAULT_FEEDBACK_THRESHOLD`), `CompileResult`, `CompileFailure`, `CompilerHooks` and the `Isolate` struct (no pub field) have core `embed:` lines with their public fields and variants, and the pub methods and trait impls (`Display`, `Error`, `Default`) of their impls in the files outside `abi/` and `builtins.rs`. The ABI hook types (`BuiltinTable`, `HostFn`, `PromiseRejectionTracker`) are core lines already. Two kinds of named types are not core: `Dispatch` (the `IsolateConfig::dispatch` field) has `embed (not core):` lines, because it is the list of dispatch expansions of H15 and H15-Q2 is open (`NOT_CORE_TYPES` in the test; decision M3-P3-H20-DISPATCH: `Dispatch` stays embed, not core, as an H15 tuning type); and the types of other crates (`HeapConfig`, `HeapError`, `VerifiedUnit`, `EvalContext`, `FunctionCtorKind`) are not read, because their crates and ADRs own them. Reason: they are the only way from an embedder into the ABI, and the `for<'s>` bound of the `Cx` scopes is the Q4 guarantee; a change to one of them changes what every embedder writes. The other `Isolate` methods (`builtin_table`, `compiler`, `dispatch`, the handles, `collect_garbage`, `verify_heap`, `gc_stats`, `string_view`) are not in the core: they run no ABI code and take no hook (`collect_garbage` runs no finalizer, H12), and they belong to the embedder API of H22, H23 and H19, with those freeze points. The test is for the methods of `Isolate` only, as the code is: the extractor marks `ENTRY_POINTS` only in `impl Isolate` blocks. So `InterruptHandle::request` is not an entry point, though its callback is a function of the embedder that runs at an interrupt poll while JS runs: `request` is a method of `InterruptHandle` (H23-Q6), not of `Isolate`, and `Isolate::interrupt_handle` takes no hook (fix round 7, RV6-A2). `with_module_host` (it takes the `resolve` and `load` hooks) and `new` (it takes the `CompilerHooks` in `IsolateConfig`) are `Isolate` methods, so they still fit the test. With `request` added to `ENTRY_POINTS` (a probe, reverted), the re-blessed golden does not change and `the_golden_has_the_embedder_entry_points` fails. They are still golden lines, marked `embed (not core):` (M3-P3 fix round 2, FP2-GOLDEN-RAW). **The golden is a tripwire** (fix round 7; decision M3-P3-H20-GOLDEN-TRIPWIRE). `h20_core.rs` reads the source text with no compiler data, and a reader of source text cannot list all of a Rust API. So the golden finds a change in the forms that it reads; it is not a complete list of the public API. Since fix round 6 (RV5-F1, RV5-S1; decision M3-P3-H20-FAILCLOSED) it reads more forms. It reads, in every `src` file of the default build: (1) every pub method and const of every inherent `impl Isolate` block, also `impl crate::Isolate` and a block with a `where` clause (the type name is read before `where`); (2) every other impl whose head names `Isolate`, as one line with its associated types, consts and method signatures: a trait impl (`impl Deref for Isolate`, `impl AsRef<Heap> for Isolate`, `impl Drop for Isolate`; none exists today) or an impl that takes it (`impl From<&Isolate> for &Heap`); (3) every free pub fn, const or static outside `abi/` whose line names `Isolate` or a raw type, in any module (today one: `export_facts`); (4) every `pub use` and `pub mod` of `lib.rs` as a `path:` line, and each re-exported item of a crate module and each pub item of a pub module (`versions`, `internals`) as a line; (5) the types that those lines name, to the end (the type closure: the type line, and the pub methods and trait impls of the impls in the files outside `abi/` and `builtins.rs` whose self type is that type), and the types that the core lines name as core lines (above). In the `abi/` files it reads every pub item and the impls whose self type is a pub `abi` type or whose trait is a pub `abi` trait. These forms are `unread:` lines, which fail `h20_core_matches_the_golden` and `the_extractor_reads_every_form`: a type alias of `Isolate` (`type IsoAlias = Isolate`, so an `impl IsoAlias` block), a `use` that renames `Isolate` or a raw type (`use crate::Isolate as Iso`), a type alias that gives a raw type another name, an impl that names `Isolate` inside a fn, block or `macro_rules!` body, a glob re-export and a module file of a pub module. The default build: an item is skipped only if a `cfg` on it, on an inline module around it or on its module in `lib.rs` is false in every default build of every target: `test`, and the features `spike-native` and `ic-stats`, which dep-guard 11 keeps out of the ep9 graph (test `only_the_off_features_are_off` reads the workspace Cargo.toml files: no crate turns them on, and the default ep9_cli build turns on `ep9_vm/jit`). A target `cfg` such as `target_pointer_width = "64"` and every other feature (`jit`, `become`) are read like a target, and the line shows the `cfg` (fix round 3, Codex C2-FP1; fix round 6, RV5-F1 M1). So a new raw producer in one of these forms (for example a raw `Value` form of `Isolate` that comes back) is a new line or an `unread:` line, and a review must bless it. A changed or removed `embed (not core):` line is not an H20 core change. Test `no_embed_line_names_a_raw_type` fails on any line but a `path:` or an `unread:` line (an `unread:` line fails `the_extractor_reads_every_form`) that names `Value`, `Heap`, `CellPtr`, `ScratchRoots` or `Slot` (fix round 5 read only the `Isolate` methods, and before it only `Value`; Codex W4-1), except two exact lines: `string_view`, and `IsolateError`, whose variant `Heap` holds a `HeapError`. The negative controls: `a_new_isolate_method_is_a_new_line` adds a method in `isolate.rs`, one in another file, four under target `cfg`s (a block, an inline module, a module of `lib.rs`) and two that give a `&Heap` and a `CellPtr`, and it checks that the gated `heap` block of `isolate.rs` gives no line; `each_way_to_add_a_raw_producer_fails_the_gate` makes one change at a time: a block under `cfg(feature = "jit")` and under `cfg(feature = "become")` (and no line under `cfg(feature = "ic-stats")`), a `where` clause, a type alias, a renaming `use` and a raw-type alias, `Deref`, `AsRef` and `From` impls, a free fn that `lib.rs` re-exports, a fn in a pub module and a static in a private module, a re-exported fn and an `Isolate` method that give a struct that holds a `&Heap`, a new `Exception` field, an impl in a fn body and a glob re-export. With the verifiers' forms M1-M5 in the real `src` (a probe, reverted), 9 of the 16 `h20_core` tests fail, `h20_core_matches_the_golden` among them. An `Isolate` method with a method-level `cfg` is still a line (the reader skips only gated blocks and modules), which errs on the safe side; and `the_cfg_reader_knows_the_default_build` checks the `cfg` reader on fixed input. The escape classes of the fix-round-5 review (RV5-F1 M1-M5: a block under `cfg(feature = "jit")`, a `where` clause, a type alias of `Isolate`, a trait impl for `Isolate`, a free fn that `lib.rs` re-exports or that a pub module has; RV5-S1) are now lines or `unread:` lines. Known escape classes that the golden does not read (a new raw producer or a changed member of a core type in them gives no line, and every `h20_core` test passes; the fix-round-6 verifiers proved (b)-(e) with probes, and the fix-round-7 verifier proved the RV7-1 form of (e), all reverted): (a) an item that a macro makes outside the core files: the extractor reads the source text without macro expansion and expands only the local `macro_rules!` calls of the core files (Codex C2-FP2, decision M3-P3-H20-GOLDEN-LIMIT; a re-exported one is a line that says so, as `Atom` is); (b) a module with a `#[path]` attribute whose file is not read, and a module file in the same places: a file outside `src/`, not named `.rs`, or whose first name under `src/` is a gated module of `lib.rs` (`tests`, `native`): the directory `src/tests/` and the file `src/native.rs` (RV6-G1, RV7-3; M3-P4 ACCEPT-8 note N2: with `#[cfg(feature = "jit")] #[path = "native.rs"] mod m;` in `lib.rs`, a probe, reverted, the raw producers of `native.rs`, such as `native_target(&Isolate, Value)`, give no line and all 16 tests pass; the same form to a new file fails 9 of them); `sources()` reads every other `.rs` file under `src/`, so a `#[path]` module to such a file is read); (c) in a file outside `abi/` and `builtins.rs`, a trait impl whose head does not name `Isolate` and whose self type is not a type of the closure (in `isolate.rs`, also not `Cx`), for example `impl From<Local<'s>> for Value`, `impl IntoKey<'s> for Value` or `impl From<Value> for Local<'s>` in `string.rs`; and in the `abi/` files and `builtins.rs`, a trait impl whose head does not name `Isolate` and whose trait and self type are not pub `abi` or `builtins.rs` items, such as `impl From<Local<'s>> for Value` or `impl From<Local<'s, FlatStr>> for JsStr<'static>` (RV6-G2, RV6-A1, RV7-2); (d) a type alias, a renaming `use` or an impl in a body for a type of the closure (`Exception`, `IsolateConfig`, ...): the `unread:` rules know only `Isolate` and the raw types (RV6-G3); (e) an impl whose self type is an `abi` type (`Local`, `Cx`, ...) in a file other than the `abi/` files and `builtins.rs` (`impl Cx` of `isolate.rs` is read) (RV6-G4), and an impl of a type of the closure (`Exception`, `IsolateConfig`, ...) in an `abi/` file or `builtins.rs`, unless it is a trait impl of a pub `abi` or `builtins.rs` trait: the type closure reads only the impls of the files outside `abi/` and `builtins.rs`, and the `abi/` reader reads only the impls of pub `abi` and `builtins.rs` types and traits (RV7-1); (f) the types of other crates (`ep9_heap`, `ep9_value`, `ep9_bytecode`; H20-Q4-X1 names the `ep9_heap` case). In every class, an impl whose head names `Isolate` is still a line, in every file (items (1) and (2)): for example `impl crate::Isolate` or `impl From<&crate::Isolate> for crate::isolate::Exception` in `abi/mod.rs` (M3-P4 ACCEPT-8 note N1; probes, reverted: each fails 8 of the 16 tests, and `impl crate::isolate::Exception` with a pub method in `abi/mod.rs` gives no line, class (e)). So the freeze of the core depends on review too: the README §3.1 review record and the M3-P4 ACCEPT-8 H20 rows check each change for the classes (a)-(f) (for (a): each new macro that emits an impl or an item that names `Isolate` or a raw type). A complete check needs compiler data (rustdoc JSON on nightly, or a public-API tool) and is M1 work: H20-Q6. **`Isolate::string_view(&mut self, v: Value)` stays** (product call, M3-P3 FREEZE-PREP step 2), not in the core: (1) it is sound for any `v` (fix round 5, Codex W4-1): it reads `v` only if `Heap::is_cell` says that a live cell of this isolate's heap starts at it (`is_cell` finishes the lazy sweep first) and the cell's kind is a string kind, so a `Value` of a freed cell, of another `ep9_heap::Heap` or of a dropped isolate, or bits that do not start a cell, give `None`; if the memory of a freed cell now holds a new live string, the view shows that string (wrong text, but an in-bounds read of a live string); and the view borrows the isolate exclusively (H19, W4-STR-VIEW-EXCL). Before fix round 5 it had no check: Codex's probes read a freed cell (a `Value` kept in a `Vec` across a GC, zap off), read past a 16-byte cell that `Heap::alloc` made, and ended with SIGSEGV (exit 139) on a `Value` of a dropped isolate and of a dropped embedder heap. Tests: `tests::strings::string_view_reads_only_live_cells_of_its_heap` (in-crate: 64 unrooted strings, a GC with zap on and off, an interior address, an address outside the cage; with the check removed it fails on the first freed string) and the `string_view` doctest with a cell of an embedder-made heap, before and after that heap drops; (2) its two `compile_fail` doctests are the H19 check of the embedder view rule, and a `cfg` gate would make them fail to compile for another reason, so they would pass with no proof; (3) its callers hold raw `Value`s by design: the spike-native SP-Unit check (`spikes/spike-b/src/unit/checks.rs`) and an `ep9_vm` unit test. A scoped no-copy view of a `Local<FlatStr>` can come later as a part-2 addition if an embedder needs one; today `Cx::to_rust_string` copies and `Cx::code_unit_at` reads one unit.

**Public paths** (M3-P3 FREEZE-PREP; closes M2-P1-FIX-NO-REEXPORT and M2-P3-ABI-REEXPORT). Each name of `ep9_vm::abi` has two public paths, `ep9_vm::abi::X` and the crate root `ep9_vm::X`, and both are in the core. The crate root re-exports the whole `abi` list: `IteratorRecord`, `ObjectClass`, `PromiseCapability`, `PromiseRejectionOperation`, `PromiseRejectionTracker` and `PromiseState`, which were only at `ep9_vm::abi`, are now at the root too (no caller changes: `ep9_builtins` uses both forms). The one exception is `ep9_vm::abi::export_facts` (V8-A13): it is not a builtin ABI name and stays at `abi::` only. A name added to `ep9_vm::abi` gets its root re-export in the same change (test `every_abi_name_has_a_crate_root_path`). The table types keep their root paths (`ep9_vm::BuiltinDef` and the others; the `builtins` module is private). `CollectionCursor` (the stack-only cursor of `collection_cursor` and `collection_next`) had no path until M3-P3 FREEZE-PREP step 2: it is `pub` in the private module `abi::collections`. Now `abi` re-exports it (one `pub use` line in `crates/ep9_vm/src/abi/mod.rs`, an orchestrator grant), and so does the crate root. The golden has no `path: (none)` line, and `the_golden_covers_the_core` fails if one comes back.

H20 has two parts (decision M2-H20-PARTS; the table filled by M3-P3 FREEZE-PREP). A Freeze table replaces the single Freeze point (README §3.4):

`Cx` and the signature of each public `Cx` method that exists at the freeze (136 at 88998a1, and 136 after M3-P3 EMBED-MIGRATE step 2 at 89fdae1, with the scoped embedder forms `run_script`, `run_module`, `global_binding` and `display`); the embedder entry points of `Isolate` (`with_cx`, `with_cx_checkpoint`, `create_realm`, `perform_microtask_checkpoint`, `take_unhandled_rejections`, `new`, `register_host_function`, `with_module_host`; not `Dispatch`, an H15 type, and not the types of other crates; M3-P3 fix round 6, RV5-F2); the table types (`BuiltinId` with its 7 + 9 bit split, `BuiltinDef`, `BuiltinKind`, `PropDef`, `PropKey`, `PropValue`, `PropAttrs` and its constants, `ConstValue`, `IntrinsicDef`, `IntrinsicValue`, `ObjectProps`, `BuiltinModule`, `BuiltinTable`, `WellKnownSymbol`, `check_tables`); When `f` is a FUNCTION cell and `args` is a tail of the host function's own arguments, it calls nothing: it writes a request into header slots of the host frame (`NEW_TARGET` f, `CONTEXT` this, `BYTECODE_OFFSET` the int32 k + 1; 0, as `push_frame` writes it, is no request) and returns a marker, the hole value. `call::call_host` then pops the host frame and calls `f` in its place: the callee frame starts at the host frame's base and the arguments shift in place, with no list, so a chain of forwards adds no host frame. Any other `f` (a bound function, a proxy, a value that is not callable) or `args` is called at once, as `call_args` does. The marker is only for the host function's own return value: the request is made only when the host function returns it, and a host function that keeps it or passes it on gives the hole value to other code (wrong values, such as `typeof` "object"; no memory fault: a probe with GC stress and the heap verifier). `Function.prototype.call` uses it; `apply` keeps `call_built` (H20-Q3). ## Consequences

- **Gains.** A `Local` costs nothing (no handle scope); a host call passes 4 integer words (cx, this, args, new_target), which fits the 4 Win64 argument registers, and returns in one register. Builtins reach the VM only through `Cx`, so `forbid(unsafe_code)` holds in `ep9_builtins`. No `Vec<Local>` is ever needed: lists are a `ScratchList`, a JS array or an `ArgsBuilder`.
- **Costs.** Every builtin spells `<'s>`. R2 is a lint plus a debug check, not a type error. `apply` copies the arguments once; `call` copies none, and its tail call costs about 58 instructions more per call (H20-Q3, 2026-11-04). The LIFO checks run at run time.
- **Costs of the tables.** A block holds at most 512 builtins, and 128 blocks exist; an id never moves, so a removed builtin keeps its slot. A table error shows at `Isolate::new`, not at compile time (the checks are cached per table).
- **Follow-ups.** Done in M0 wk4: gc-lint and the debug check (P2-LINT); the symbol entry points and `%Symbol.prototype%` (P2-SYM merge); accessors in `define_own_property` and `PropValue::Accessor` installs (P3-ACC); the builtins of `TEMPLATES.md` 1-10 and the `@@iterator` protocol (P3-BLTA, P3-BLTB, P3-NAT). Done in M0 month 2 P1: index access (ABI-1) and the iterator protocol (ABI-3). Done in M0 month 3 P1: H22 realms for R5 (REALMS). Done in M0 month 3 P3: the Freeze table, the public paths (with `CollectionCursor`), the two-realm R5 test and the core golden (FREEZE-PREP); the raw `Value` forms of `Isolate` removed (EMBED-MIGRATE) and H20-Q4 filled. Open: H18 element storage for the v0 limits above; the async GetIterator and GetMethod with a well-known symbol (part-2 additions for the builtins that need them). The core freezes at M0 exit (Freeze table).

| H20-Q3 | `call`/`apply` without the copy | M1 | One copy now (`call_args`, `ArgsBuilder` into the callee frame); a tail-call host path in M1, as V8's Function.prototype.call shifts the arguments and tail-calls **Filled 2026-11-04 (M6-P3 H20Q; as built): `call` has the tail-call host path, `apply` keeps its one copy.** `Function.prototype.call` returns `cx.tail_call_args(func, thisArg, args.rest(1))` (part-2 row "Tail calls of host functions"): its arguments shift in place into the callee frame, and its host frame takes no stack room while the callee runs. Data (aarch64-apple-darwin, release, `EP9_HASH_SEED=1`, against 39788b53): recursion through `.call` reaches depth 69,901 at the default 64 MiB native stack (40,327 before; direct recursion 80,655); a loop of 2,000,000 `.call`s retires 2,778M instructions (2,662M before: about 58 more per call, the request and the second call entry); BENCH-SET at c7aa0118 (`.github/scripts/perf-ci-v0.mjs`, the instruction medians, two rounds): raytrace +0.09% and +0.18%, deltablue +0.12% and +0.17%, every workload at most +0.24% (limit +0.5%). `apply` keeps CreateListFromArrayLike into an `ArgsBuilder` and one copy into the callee frame, as V8 copies the list to the stack: a tail form of `apply` (the list moved down over the host frame) gave raytrace +0.93% and no deeper recursion (36,155 both), so it was not kept; `Reflect.apply` (not an H20Q file) is the same. Not done (M2): a bytecode callee of a tail call still runs in a nested dispatch run, one native level per `.call`, as from `call_function_object`; a call in the same run needs the interpreter's call path (`crates/ep9_vm/src/interp/slow/call.rs`). **Filled 2026-11-06 (M7-P0 CALLHOST; as built): the rest.** A call of `%Function.prototype.apply%` or `%Function.prototype.call%` (`IntrinsicId` 93-94) with a bytecode callee of the same realm pushes the callee frame in the same dispatch run (part-2 row "Tail calls of host functions", the 2026-11-06 note); `apply` copies its list once, from the Array or the arguments object straight into the callee frame. Every other case (a bound function, a Proxy, a class constructor, another realm, a hole, a changed `length`, an accessor, a spread or prefixed call) runs the builtin. Also a host callee in one of the 9 fixed call shapes (`interp/slow/call.rs` `host_entry`) skips `decode_call`. Data (aarch64-apple-darwin, release, `EP9_HASH_SEED=1`, against 92f2d37f): recursion through `.call` reaches depth 87,380 (86,029 before; direct recursion 104,856), through `.apply(null, arguments)` 65,534 (36,157 before) and through `.apply(null, array)` 69,903 (37,449 before); a loop of 2,000,000 `.call`s retires 2,016M instructions (3,406M before), of `.apply(null, [1, 2])` 2,294M (3,885M before), and of `g.apply(null, arguments)` in a callee 4,380M (5,928M before); BENCH-SET (the 21 workloads of `.github/scripts/perf-ci-v0.mjs`, `ep9-bench --counter time --runs 5 --warmup 1`, the instruction medians, two rounds, order flipped): raytrace -17.98% both rounds, deltablue -3.35% and -3.36%, every workload at most +0.01% (limit +0.5%) |

On an embedder path it knows only the base list `STACK_ONLY` (`Local`, `Args`, `Rest`, `ArgsBuilder`, `ScratchList`, `PropertyDescriptor`, `JsStr`, `FlatStr`); it learns that a type holds a `Local` (`PromiseCapability`, `IteratorRecord`, `CollectionCursor`) only from the files that define it (RV6-A4). So `cargo xtask gc-lint <embedder path>` finds `Vec<Local<'s>>` but not `Vec<PromiseCapability<'s>>`, `Vec<IteratorRecord<'s>>` or `Box<PromiseCapability<'s>>` (fix round 7: 1 finding), and `cargo xtask gc-lint <embedder path> crates/ep9_vm/src` finds all 4, the debug on-stack check in `Local::get` checks only the place of the `Local` that is read, and a `Cx` method takes a `Local` by value, so the copy on the stack passes it (`cx.string_len(v[0])`), and the GC-stress runs find the rest in the tests. Embedders must keep each `Local` on the native stack and can run `cargo xtask gc-lint <their paths> crates/ep9_vm/src` (the `ep9_vm` sources are needed for the types that hold a `Local`). Data: 10 x `JSON.stringify` of 20,000 objects of 4 fields takes 0.15 s user at 39788b53 and at this head [2026-11-05, spec-temporal B4: `[[BigIntData]]` is built: `primitive_data` gives the BigInt of a BigInt wrapper, and JSON SerializeJSONProperty step 4.d unwraps it (then step 10 throws the TypeError); `tests/primitive_wrappers.rs` has a BigInt wrapper line (with a throwing `valueOf` and `toString` that never run)] |

## Reopens if

- A GC-stress failure is traced to a `Local` in Rust heap memory: add a type-aware dylint lint (ABI-5 e).
- The JIT/AOT host-call stub needs more than 4 integer arguments on Win64.

So a walk of 8 steps or fewer takes no unit, the last 1 to 8 steps of a longer walk take none, a walk that uses up a budget of 1 or more runs at most 7 steps past it, and one that starts at 0 or below runs 8 steps (`call_bytecode` in call.rs takes its unit at line 496, after its `poll` at line 470, so a callee can start at 0). A miss goes to the cold path: `property::instance_of` reaches `prototype_walk_step`, which takes a unit and polls at 0 or below at its first step.
